hints: Look carefully at what each statement is testing, from acid-base behaviour to solubility, electron counting and shape.
Remember that ammonia is liberated from ammonium salts by a strong base, and that silver chloride, bromide and iodide behave very differently in ammonia.
Count the total electrons in the ammonium ion and in methane, remembering to subtract one for the positive charge, and recall the true shape of the ammonium ion.
walkthrough:
**Test the acid-base claim**

Think like a Brønsted-Lowry chemist. Ammonium is the conjugate acid of ammonia, so base removes a proton to give ammonia.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Test the silver iodide claim**

Recall the classic silver halide test with aqueous ammonia. Solubility decreases down the group.

$$\text{AgCl soluble in dilute } \text{NH}_3, \text{ AgBr soluble in concentrated } \text{NH}_3, \text{ AgI insoluble}$$

**Count electrons for isoelectronic check**

Count all electrons, then adjust for charge. Nitrogen has 7 electrons and each hydrogen has 1.

$$\text{For } \text{NH}_4^+: 7 + (4 \times 1) - 1 = 10 \text{ electrons}$$
$$\text{For } \text{CH}_4: 6 + (4 \times 1) = 10 \text{ electrons}$$

**Check shape and bonding**

Ammonium is formed when $\text{NH}_3$ donates its lone pair to $\text{H}^+$, so it does contain one dative covalent bond. But with four bonding pairs and no lone pairs, VSEPR gives a tetrahedral shape, not square planar.

options.A: Incorrect. A strong acid would protonate any $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{NH}_4^+$, not liberate it. Ammonia gas is released when an ammonium salt is warmed with a strong base such as $\text{NaOH}$.
options.B: Incorrect. Silver iodide is insoluble even in concentrated aqueous ammonia. Only $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute ammonia and $\text{AgBr}$ dissolves in concentrated ammonia.
options.C: Correct. $\text{NH}_4^+$ has 10 electrons and $\text{CH}_4$ also has 10 electrons, so they are isoelectronic. This also explains why both are tetrahedral.
options.D: Incorrect. The ammonium ion does contain a dative covalent bond from $\text{NH}_3$ to $\text{H}^+$, but it is tetrahedral, not square planar. Square planar is the trap word here.
